capabilities: Visualize a folder of Markdown cards as crystal structures linked by [[wikilink]] lines
Read PDFs, images and Markdown in a draggable desktop of windows
Create and rename cards from a sidebar while reading a document
Write and delete [[links]] by dragging connection lines between cards
Review cards with content hidden in recall mode
extras: README is written in Chinese with a separate English README (README.en.md); the CrystalFloat companion is a separate ~107 MB download; a warning notes that dot-file sync channels like Obsidian Sync will not carry the .crystal-boxes.json files, so box layouts stay device-local under those sync setups.
intentEvidence: 它不是更好的图谱，是不同的起点。
motivation: The author found that graph view answers 'who does this note relate to' and turns everything into a tangle, while readers need to see what a block of knowledge contains and how far it has grown.
problem: Obsidian's graph view starts from individual notes and ignores folder structure, so readers who organize knowledge by subject and chapter lose sight of a block's structure while reading.

summary: Visual knowledge tool that lays out a folder of Markdown cards as linked crystals, with a PDF and image reader and note-taking side by side.
